# INTRODUCTION

This doc shows **job count location quotients** for Sheffield, Barnsley, Doncaster and Rotherham for **sectors that are part of the UK Industrial Strategy definition list** (see below for more info on that).

-   For BRES, Barnsley, Doncaster and Rotherham are combined (BRES still uses ITL3 2021 zones where those three are in one zone).
-   For Companies House data (job counts extracted from accounts between June 2024 to end of June 2025), each of the four places have separate plots.

# EXISTING (OR RECENTLY ENDED) UKRI CCI CLUSTERS

Original projects:

-   “[Business of Fashion, Textiles and Technology](https://bftt.org.uk/)” has centres in London, Cambs, Chelsea, Leeds, Loughborough. (“[Future Fashion Factory](https://futurefashionfactory.org/)” is a cluster based at Leeds University Institute of Textiles and Colour.)
-   [Creative Industries Policy and Evidence Centre](https://pec.ac.uk/) (Newcastle University, with ‘Southern hub’): policy research+exchange across all CCI.
-   [Future Screens NI](https://www.futurescreens.org/): “delivering expert technical skills, opportunity and growth across film and broadcast, animation, games and immersive technologies and industries in Northern Ireland.” (Queens and University of Ulster.)
-   [Creative informatics](https://creativeinformatics.org/) (Edinburgh): “Funding and development opportunities to creative individuals and organisations working in Edinburgh and Southeast Scotland that want to develop new products, businesses and experiences using data and data-driven technology.”
-   [InGame](https://innovationforgames.com/): R&D in Dundee’s games cluster.
-   [XR Stories](https://xrstories.co.uk/) (University of York): Extended reality research with industry, lab at York University.

More recent projects funded (Nov 2024 announcement):

-   [Music Futures](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/institute-of-popular-music/projects/music-futures/) in Liverpool.
-   [Createch Frontiers](https://www.bcu.ac.uk/research/createch-frontiers), Birmingham City, Coventry and Warwick Universities.

Funding period ended:

-   [Bath/Bristol Creative R&D](https://bristolbathcreative.org/): screen / performance / publishing (ended 2024)
-   [Clwstwr](https://clwstwr.org.uk/) in Cardiff (ended): “Creates platforms for independent companies, SMEs, micro-businesses and freelancers to compete with global media companies.” (Some Bath/Bristol overlap)
-   [StoryFutures](https://www.storyfutures.com/) (Surrey, Royal Holloway University, ended): “placing innovative storytelling at the heart of the next generation of immersive technologies and experiences.”

# UK INDUSTRIAL STRATEGY LINKAGE

The [UK Industrial Strategy](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/the-uks-modern-industrial-strategy-2025) was released in 2025, with accompanying plans for 6 out of the 8 target "IS-8" sectors. It also has a [sector definition list](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/industrial-strategy/industrial-strategy-sector-definitions-list) that provides SIC codes being targeted - top level sectors and 'frontier' subsectors (a few of which overlap; most do not). These range in specificity between 2 digit and 5 digit SIC codes.

As that webpage says, most of these SIC codes cannot capture the full range of possible firms the strategy aims to cover, and it also contains entire sections that SIC codes can't cover at all - clean energy and certain digital sectors in particular. However, it does allow an analysis of which sectors are *definitely* within those industrial strategy categories. This section gathers job details for those specific sectors - a distinct range of types and breadth - and compares South Yorkshire to the rest of the UK where possible, to see which sectors align with the industrial strategy and other analysis above. This is done for both BRES and Companies House job counts, to pick up on different job types.

The table below lists the IS-8 broad sector headings. In the IndStrat plots, the abbreviations for these IS-8 headings appear before the sector name. Clean energy - as mentioned above - has no SIC codes and so can't currently be matched.

```{r brad_indstrattable}

indstrat <- tibble(
  `IS8 sector` = c(
    'Advanced Manufacturing',
    'Clean Energy Industries',
    'Creative Industries',
    'Defence',
    'Digital and Technologies', 
    'Financial Services',
    'Life Sciences', 
    'Professional and Business Services'),
  `Abbreviation` = c(
    'ADV MANUF',
    '--',
    'CREATIVE',
    'DEFENCE',
    'DIGITAL',
    'FIN',
    'LIFESCI',
    'PBS'
    )
)

#escape = FALSE so that markdown in the cells (the links) is rendered correctly.
knitr::kable(indstrat, escape = FALSE, caption = "Table: Industrial Strategy IS-8 names and abbreviations (dashes mean that sector doesn't appear for South Yorkshire)")

```

# History of CCI jobs and GVA in South Yorkshire

## CCI jobs as a percent of the total for core cities and South Yorkshire

Here, job counts from BRES are summed for all industrial strategy creative SIC codes to find how the percent of South Yorkshire's CCI jobs has changed over the data's history, alongside Great Britain core cities for comparison. BRES has data from 2015 to 2024 - a 3 year running average is used here to smooth its volatility.

A couple of things to note here:

-   Sheffield's CCI job count is in a lower core city group with three others, percentage-wise: Birmingham, Liverpool and Nottingham.

-   In all core cities, CCI jobs as a proportion of each city's total jobs has been climbing, including through COVID for most, though not all.

-   Barnsley, Doncaster and Rotherham are here for comparison, but are not similar to other core cities and so not too much should be read into their position here (same for the GVA plot below).

```{r, fig-ccijobs}
#| fig-height: 6

cciplot = readRDS('../local/cciplot.rds')

# Loading this here to get order of colours - GVA covers UK so includes Belfast
sections.plot = readRDS('../local/cci_gva_plot.rds')

n <- length(unique(sections.plot$Region_name))
set.seed(12)
qual_col_pals = brewer.pal.info[brewer.pal.info$category == 'qual',]
col_vector = unlist(mapply(brewer.pal, qual_col_pals$maxcolors, rownames(qual_col_pals)))
# pie(rep(1,n), col=sample(col_vector, n))

# randomcols <- sample(col_vector, n)
# n <- length(unique(itl3.sections.cv$SIC07_description))
randomcols <- col_vector[12:(12+(n-1))]

# Need to have two different names in the unique list to colour them correctly. Faff!
uniquesforjobs = as.character(unique(sections.plot$Region_name))

uniquesforjobs[qg('cardiff',uniquesforjobs)] = 'Cardiff'
uniquesforjobs[qg('tyne',uniquesforjobs)] = 'Newcastle upon Tyne'

#Get colours same for same SIC codes
#https://stackoverflow.com/a/33144808/5023561
#Make different pastel-ish colours
# n <- length(unique(cciplot$GEOGRAPHY_NAME))
# set.seed(15)
# qual_col_pals = brewer.pal.info[brewer.pal.info$category == 'qual',]
# col_vector = unlist(mapply(brewer.pal, qual_col_pals$maxcolors, rownames(qual_col_pals)))
# pie(rep(1,n), col=sample(col_vector, n))

# randomcols <- sample(col_vector, n)
# n <- length(unique(itl3.sections.cv$SIC07_description))
# randomcols <- col_vector[12:(12+(n-1))]

# PLOOOOT
ggplot(cciplot %>% 
         filter(!is.na(percent_indstrat_cci_movingav)) %>% 
         mutate(is_sy = qg('sheff|barnsl|doncast|rotherh',GEOGRAPHY_NAME)),
       aes(x = DATE, y = percent_indstrat_cci_movingav, 
                   colour = GEOGRAPHY_NAME, size = is_sy
                   # colour = fct_reorder(GEOGRAPHY_NAME,-percent_indstrat_cci_movingav) 
           )) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(0.5,2)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = setNames(randomcols,
                                       # unique(sections.plot$Region_name)
                                       uniquesforjobs

  # scale_color_manual(values = setNames(randomcols,unique(cciplot$GEOGRAPHY_NAME))) +
    # scale_color_manual(values = randomcols) +
  # scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2013,2017,2019,2021,2023)) +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +

  ggtitle('CCI jobs: percent of total for core cities and SY\n3 year moving average')


```

## CCI GVA as a percent of the total for core cities and South Yorkshire

Economic output for CCI sectors has to use a slightly different sector list, as the regional GVA data only has '58-60' and '90-91' SIC codes at ITL3 level (the level that most closely matches local authorities).

But it's close enough to give an indication of how CCI output has changed over time. While this data goes back much further, to 1998, it is show here for the same time range as the BRES data, for direct comparison. Again, a 3 year smoothed average is used and core cities included for comparison.

-   Out of core cities, Sheffield and Tyneside (the ITL3 zone) have historically had the lowest proportion of their economies made up by CCI sectors.

```{r, fig-ccigva}
#| fig-height: 6

# Save for qml
# sections.plot = readRDS('../local/cci_gva_plot.rds')

# PLOOOOT
ggplot(sections.plot %>%
         filter(!is.na(sector_regional_percent_movingav), year >= 2016) %>% 
         mutate(is_sy = qg('sheff|barnsl|doncast|rotherh',Region_name)),
       aes(x = year, 
           y = sector_regional_percent_movingav,
           # y = sector_regional_proportion,
           colour = Region_name, size = is_sy
           )) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  # scale_color_manual(values = randomcols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = setNames(randomcols,unique(sections.plot$Region_name))) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(0.5,2)) +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  guides(size = F) +
  xlab('year') +
  ylab('CCI GVA: percent of total GVA') +
  ggtitle('CCI GVA: percent of total GVA for core cities and SY\n3 year moving average')






```

# Location quotient plots

The outputs below use **location quotient plots**. Here's a guide to reading them:

-   Location quotients for sectoral GVA in the selected region
-   Sectors to the right of the blue line are more concentrated in this region when compared to the national average. (e.g. LQ = 10, it is 10x more concentrated)
-   Green circles have been increasing in concentration over time (larger circles increasing the most)
-   Red circles have been decreasing in concentration over time (larger circles decreasing the most)
-   Black horizontal lines show the min and max of concentration in the data’s history (from 2015 to 2023) (so, often, large green circles will be at the right of this line because sector concentration has been increasing and is continuing)
-   Per sector job counts and percent of the full IndStrat jobcount are shown on the right (not percent of entire regional jobs)
-   Fainter background squares are other place's LQs (ITL3 zones for BRES, local authorities for Companies House data)

Also:

-   The LQ plots only shows IndStrat SIC sectors where South Yorkshire has 100+ employees (for 2021-23 average)
-   And breaks them down into 'frontier' sectors and the others (a few of which overlap) - see the definitions web link above for a full explanation of those.

# SHEFFIELD

## "Frontier" SIC sectors

### BRES frontier sectors

```{r, fig-bresindstrat}

# Filter to just creative sectors
# islq <- readRDS('../local/islq2024.rds') %>% filter(toplevelindstrat %in% c(greplsector,'LIFESCI'))
# yeartoplot <- readRDS('../local/is_bres_yeartoplot2024.rds') %>% filter(toplevelindstrat %in% c(greplsector,'LIFESCI'))

# Maybe more correct ones
# islq = readRDS('../local/lqs_for_indstrat.rds') 
# yeartoplot = readRDS('../local/yeartoplots_for_indstrat.rds')
islq = readRDS('../local/lqs_for_indstrat.rds') %>% filter(qg(greplsector,sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo))
yeartoplot = readRDS('../local/yeartoplots_for_indstrat.rds') %>% filter(qg(greplsector,sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo))

# islq = readRDS('../local/lqs_for_indstrat.rds') %>% filter(toplevelindstrat %in% c(greplsector,'LIFESCI'))
# yeartoplot = readRDS('../local/yeartoplots_for_indstrat.rds')%>% filter(toplevelindstrat %in% c(greplsector,'LIFESCI'))

place = "Sheffield"

sectorLQorder <- islq %>% filter(
  DATE == max(DATE),#use latest data
  GEOGRAPHY_NAME == place) %>% 
  arrange(-LQ) %>% 
  select(sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo) %>% 
  pull()

# Tick
# length(sectorLQorder)
# length(unique(sectorLQorder))

#Split by frontier or not

#Turn the sector column into a factor and order by LQs
yeartoplot$sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo <- factor(yeartoplot$sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo, levels = sectorLQorder, ordered = T)

#Remove some LQs
yeartoplot.lqfiltered <- yeartoplot %>% filter(LQ > 0 & LQ < 100, JOBCOUNT >= minjobs)

#Drop any sectors that Bradford now doesn't have after that filter
sectorstokeep <- yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(GEOGRAPHY_NAME == place) %>% select(sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo) %>% pull

yeartoplot.lqfiltered <- yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo %in% sectorstokeep)

# Make base layer just of labelled core cities
# Remove sheffield also, don't want that labelled
corecities_baselayer = yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(GEOGRAPHY_NAME %in% corecities[!qg('sheffield',corecities)])

# Add in placename abbreviations
corecities_baselayer = corecities_baselayer %>% 
  mutate(
    placename_short = str_sub(GEOGRAPHY_NAME,1,2)
  )

# debugonce(LQ_baseplot)
p <- LQ_baseplot(df = corecities_baselayer %>% filter(is_frontier == 1), alpha = 0.8, shape = 0, sector_name = sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo, LQ_column = LQ, change_over_time = slope, labelcolumn = placename_short)

p <- addplacename_to_LQplot(df = yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(is_frontier == 1), plot_to_addto = p, 
                            placename = place, shapenumber = 16,
                            min_LQ_all_time = min_LQ_all_time,max_LQ_all_time = max_LQ_all_time,#Include minmax
                            value_column = JOBCOUNT, sector_regional_proportion = sector_regional_proportion,
                            region_name = GEOGRAPHY_NAME,
                            sector_name = sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo, change_over_time = slope, LQ_column = LQ,
                            text = 7, value_col_ismoney = F)

p <- p + 
  # coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1,7)) +
  ggtitle("IndStrat frontier sector")

p


```

```{r, fig-bresindstratd}

place = "Doncaster"

sectorLQorder <- islq %>% filter(
  DATE == max(DATE),#use latest data
  GEOGRAPHY_NAME == place) %>% 
  arrange(-LQ) %>% 
  select(sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo) %>% 
  pull()

# Tick
# length(sectorLQorder)
# length(unique(sectorLQorder))

#Split by frontier or not

#Turn the sector column into a factor and order by LQs
yeartoplot$sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo <- factor(yeartoplot$sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo, levels = sectorLQorder, ordered = T)

#Remove some LQs
yeartoplot.lqfiltered <- yeartoplot %>% filter(LQ > 0 & LQ < 100, JOBCOUNT >= minjobs)

#Drop any sectors that Bradford now doesn't have after that filter
sectorstokeep <- yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(GEOGRAPHY_NAME == place) %>% select(sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo) %>% pull

yeartoplot.lqfiltered <- yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo %in% sectorstokeep)

# Make base layer just of labelled core cities
corecities_baselayer = yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(GEOGRAPHY_NAME %in% corecities)

# Add in placename abbreviations
corecities_baselayer = corecities_baselayer %>% 
  mutate(
    placename_short = str_sub(GEOGRAPHY_NAME,1,2)
  )

# debugonce(LQ_baseplot)
p <- LQ_baseplot(df = corecities_baselayer %>% filter(is_frontier == 1), alpha = 0.8, shape = 0, sector_name = sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo, LQ_column = LQ, change_over_time = slope, labelcolumn = placename_short)

p <- addplacename_to_LQplot(df = yeartoplot.lqfiltered %>% filter(is_frontier == 1), plot_to_addto = p, 
                            placename = place, shapenumber = 16,
                            min_LQ_all_time = min_LQ_all_time,max_LQ_all_time = max_LQ_all_time,#Include minmax
                            value_column = JOBCOUNT, sector_regional_proportion = sector_regional_proportion,
                            region_name = GEOGRAPHY_NAME,
                            sector_name = sic_namefrom_indstrat_combo, change_over_time = slope, LQ_column = LQ,
                            text = 7, value_col_ismoney = F)

p <- p + 
  # coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1,7)) +
  ggtitle("IndStrat frontier sector")

p
```
